claim_dispositions.claim: God’s providence makes the brothers morally blameless
claim_dispositions.reason: Genesis 45 and 50 preserve their harmful intention while also attributing preservation to God.

claim_dispositions.claim: “Father to Pharaoh” certainly names a specific Egyptian office
claim_dispositions.reason: Courtly counsel/honorific rhetoric is possible; no exact title identification is secure.

claim_dispositions.claim: Goshen has one certain archaeological identification
claim_dispositions.reason: Broad eastern Delta context only; exact location is debated.

claim_dispositions.claim: Genesis 46 totals are solved by adding unnamed travelers
claim_dispositions.reason: Represent MT, LXX, Qumran Exodus evidence, and Acts 7 without invented people.

claim_dispositions.claim: Egyptian shepherd aversion equals modern racial segregation
claim_dispositions.reason: Narrative social-boundary wording does not establish that modern category or a certain historical cause.

claim_dispositions.claim: Rameses terminology by itself dates the whole narrative
claim_dispositions.reason: Later familiar nomenclature and other geographic/compositional possibilities remain.

claim_dispositions.claim: Egyptian records independently verify Joseph’s famine policy
claim_dispositions.reason: Comparative land-tenure evidence is limited and does not attest the story’s exact policy.

claim_dispositions.claim: Genesis 47 straightforwardly describes modern chattel slavery
claim_dispositions.reason: Land tenure, service, dependency, labor, and later chattel categories must be distinguished.

claim_dispositions.claim: Ephraim and Manasseh’s status is identical to a known legal adoption contract
claim_dispositions.reason: The narrative elevates them in tribal inheritance without specifying that modern or exact institutional equivalence.

claim_dispositions.claim: The angel/messenger in Genesis 48 is explicitly Jesus in the immediate text
claim_dispositions.reason: The Hebrew divine-agency language does not require an explicit Trinitarian identification.

claim_dispositions.claim: Genesis 49:10 has one undisputed Hebrew reading
claim_dispositions.reason: Several philological and translation options remain live.

claim_dispositions.claim: Genesis 49 is exclusively predictive prophecy without tribal/historical dimension
claim_dispositions.reason: Genre includes poetic blessing, tribal characterization, history, and future-oriented speech.

claim_dispositions.claim: Judah’s saying has only later Christian messianic meaning
claim_dispositions.reason: Immediate tribal and royal language and later Jewish/Christian reception are distinct.

claim_dispositions.claim: Genesis 49 proves one exact Pentateuchal composition date
claim_dispositions.reason: Composition and dating approaches are diverse; no one verse settles the whole Pentateuch.

claim_dispositions.claim: Jacob certainly received full royal embalming
claim_dispositions.reason: The text says physicians embalmed him but does not describe full royal protocol.

claim_dispositions.claim: The brothers’ report of Jacob’s forgiveness command is certainly fabricated
claim_dispositions.reason: The text reports their message but does not independently verify it or call it false.

claim_dispositions.claim: Genesis 50:20 makes all evil morally neutral
claim_dispositions.reason: The verse preserves human evil intention and divine good purpose; it does not neutralize wrongdoing.

claim_dispositions.claim: Joseph’s tomb or coffin has been archaeologically identified
claim_dispositions.reason: Genesis ends with his coffin in Egypt; no archaeological identification is established.
